title: Claude Raises Proven Share of Riemann Zeta Zeros on the Critical Line to 67.25%
whyItMatters: Jumped the unconditional lower bound on Riemann zeta zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.25%—a massive leap over decades of 0.1%-scale incremental improvements.
summary: Asked to take a serious run at the Riemann Hypothesis, an unreleased Anthropic Claude research model instead discovered a Lean-verified analytic proof raising the unconditional proportion of nontrivial Riemann zeta zeros proved to lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2 from 41.6% to 67.25%. Analytic number theorists Brian Conrey, Dan Goldston, and Youness Lamzouri examined the argument, with Lamzouri confirming correctness and publishing a simplified exposition.
technicalHighlights: Shattered decades of sub-percentage incremental improvements (Conrey 40% → Pratt–Robles–Zaharescu–Zeindler 41.7% → Claude 67.25%).
Passed Lean 4 comparator verification and underwent independent review by leading analytic number theorists.
Served as an immediate technical stepping stone toward Anthropic’s November 2026 Lean proof of GRH.
caveats: Did not settle the full Riemann Hypothesis on its own; Anthropic noted at release that the specific mollifier techniques alone would not reach 100%.

scoreRationale.foundational: Achieved the largest single jump in critical-line zeta zero proportions in analytic number theory history.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly catalyzed new analytic tools and momentum leading to the November 2026 Lean Riemann proof.
scoreRationale.verification: Passed Lean comparator checks and received independent confirmation from Conrey, Goldston, and Lamzouri.
scoreRationale.velocity: Improved a fiercely contested analytic bound by +25.6 percentage points in a single AI research campaign.
